summary: The main article describes a visible light mediated iridium photocatalysed reverse polarity Povarov reaction. It includes one optimization table, two schemes detailing the scope and mechanistic investigations, and a final scheme proposing the reaction mechanism involving proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET).

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Previous reports in the context of this work. PC = photocatalyst.
items.description: Illustrates the reverse polarity platform for amine synthesis and previous work by Chen/Dixon and Hirano/Miura.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of photocatalytic reverse polarity Povarov reaction
items.description: Lists reaction conditions including Hantzsch ester loading, light source, and yields for the optimization of the Povarov reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scope of the photocatalytic reverse polarity Povarov reaction. Reaction time: a 16 h, b 40 h, c 64 h.
items.description: Displays the substrate scope for the synthesis of various tetrahydroquinoline derivatives and a three-component one-pot process.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Investigation into the diastereoselectivity of the reaction.
items.description: Shows experiments regarding product epimerization and the monitoring of diastereomeric ratio over time.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Control and mechanistic experiments.
items.description: Details control experiments using amine reagents and products as initiators to probe the reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Scheme 5
items.caption: Postulated mechanism for the visible light mediated reverse polarity Povarov reaction with key PCET processes highlighted. HE = Hantzsch ester, HP = Hantzsch pyridine.
items.description: Proposes a catalytic cycle involving initiation by Hantzsch ester and a radical chain process for product formation.
